detailedExplanation: Verified against The Tiffin Girls’ School Year 9 Physics Curriculum Outline 2026–27 and aligned to AQA GCSE Physics 8463.
All objects emit and absorb infrared radiation. The hotter an object is, the greater the rate at which it emits infrared radiation.

Surface finish affects infrared behaviour. Dark, matt surfaces are generally good absorbers and good emitters; light, shiny surfaces are generally poor absorbers and emitters and are good reflectors of infrared.

A Leslie cube demonstrates that different surface finishes at the same temperature emit infrared at different rates. The comparison must be made with surfaces at the same temperature and with the detector held at a consistent distance and orientation.
Infrared radiation is an electromagnetic wave, so it can transfer energy through a vacuum. This distinguishes radiation from conduction and convection, which require matter.
examTips: For Leslie-cube questions, mention same temperature, same distance and the effect of surface finish on emission.
